trust_decision.summary: Whether the (case-insensitive) request hostname is the app whose per-app ACL applies is decided by raw string equality in AccessControlsService.lookupStaticACLs (and re-implemented in the Docker and Kubernetes label providers); a mismatch returns nil ACLs, the user-allow rule abstains and the default 'allow' policy then lets any authenticated user in.

landing_point.why: The report says the per-app ACL is matched case-sensitively against the hostname; the first place an engineer looks is the static-config lookup, where 'config.Config.Domain == domain' and 'strings.SplitN(domain, ".", 2)[0] == app' compare the raw proxy-supplied host against the configured values.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Docker and Kubernetes label providers are opt-in ACL sources (labelProvider=docker|kubernetes, internal/model/config.go:107); the advisory and report describe static per-app ACL config, so a solver can call the provider matching a separate feature and leave its case-sensitive comparison untouched.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The app-name subdomain fallback must keep resolving an app whose config.domain points at a different host, and an exact domain match must still win over a name match; a fix that replaces the fallback with exact canonical-domain equality breaks deployments that configure apps by name only.

O6_input_shapes: mixed-case hostname against a lowercase configured domain (fix.diff:252-259)
mixed-case app key in the name fallback, e.g. aPp.example.com vs APP (fix.diff:270-276)
non-ASCII / IDNA hostname vs punycode, bücher.example.com vs xn--bcher-kva.example.com (fix.diff:225-245, fix.diff:1810-1821)
scheme-qualified URL where scheme and effective port are compared (fix.diff:1585-1601, fix.diff:1767-1808)
nested subdomain resolved by app name, foo.sub.example.com (fix.diff:262-267)
IP-literal host, rejected rather than matched (fix.diff:1969-1981)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third label provider (e.g. Nomad/ECS/Podman/compose labels) plugged into the LabelProvider interface
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The interface plus this switch already host two providers with auto-detection, so adding another ACL transport is the project's natural extension point and would need the same canonicalised host match.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fourth proxy-context extractor for another proxy dialect that supplies the host with a different shape (scheme, port, userinfo)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ForwardAuth, ExtAuthz and AuthRequest already exist as three separate host producers (header, request host, parsed x-original-url), so a new dialect is a realistic maintenance addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second decoder that feeds the same model.Apps ACL schema from another source (ConfigMap, file, API)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Docker labels and ingress annotations already both flow through this one generic 'tinyauth.apps.*' decoder, so a new source would reuse it without any hostname normalisation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared hostname-canonicalising helper next to GetCookieDomain that cookie logic and ACL lookup both call
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Hostname normalisation (ToLower, IP rejection, publicsuffix handling) already lives in this file, and the published fix created a second copy of IP-rejection in pkg/validators.
